summary: A directly relevant screen-face reference with named animation staff and original studio-published GIFs.

observations.text: Doucet says the design deliberately avoided a mouth and stretching faces, leaving the eyes as its main expressive feature.

The inspected celebration GIF frame combines two upward blue eye arcs with lifted hands and an upright body. The face has no separately drawn pupil, brow or mouth; the silhouette reinforces the eye expression.

The Rescue Mission team reports that conventional cartoon exaggeration required timing adjustments for VR. They also describe bosses becoming vulnerable and silly as the player hits back, making expression a response to progress in the encounter.
Jamie Smith describes studying children's excited actions, including jumping, to build playfulness into animation.

mistIdeas: Our inference: test a small eye-shape vocabulary on MIST's existing face before adding extra facial features. Pair each shape with one readable head or body attitude.
Our inference: make a completed action trigger a held pleased shape, followed by a small recovery. Do not run the entire expressive vocabulary as an idle loop.
Our inference: use a blink at a change of attention or after a completed reaction, then let the new gaze settle. This is a proposed MIST experiment, not a verified Astro blink rule.

title: Webbed: greeting and dance as social expression

people.name: Riley Neville
people.role: Programming, Art, Sound and Game Design

summary: A tiny spider remains socially readable through visible eyes, orientation and raised front limbs; the developer provides original greeting and dance GIFs.

observations.text: In the greeting GIF's inspected frame, the spider sits directly beside another insect under its speech balloon. The small bright eye marks remain visible against the dark face, while proximity makes the interaction legible.
The dance GIF's inspected frame shows the spider leaning with front limbs raised beside a much larger moth. The face occupies very little of the image; the limb silhouette supplies a stronger signal.
Neville describes the spider's dance as a wiggle-arms move and discusses procedurally animated characters in the GameMaker interview.

mistIdeas: Our inference: make a greeting a brief acknowledgement of the arriving person, with a held look and one small gesture. The social target matters more than adding a large smile.
Our inference: test MIST reactions at the smallest intended display size. If the face becomes hard to read, reinforce the same intent through a body tilt rather than adding tiny facial detail.
Our inference: reserve an energetic celebration for meaningful success; return to a settled attentive pose after it.

title: Botanicula: tiny eyes, unusual bodies and group staging

people.name: Jaromír Plachý
people.role: Animator and creator of Botanicula, as described on Amanita's official forum index

summary: The botanical cast shows how much character can survive when faces are a few tiny marks on strongly different bodies.

observations.text: In screenshot 04, several small protagonists cluster together on a branch opposite a huge hanging dark creature. Tiny bright eyes, very different body proportions and the distance between groups carry the scene; a detailed human face is unnecessary.

Screenshot 03 repeats a one-eyed creature at different sizes. The large foreground eye gives a clear directional cue, while the surrounding small versions retain the same instantly readable eye-and-body arrangement.
In the archived IndieCade interview, Plachý and Stehlík describe nature and an old garden as inspiration; they also say the musicians saw animations during the collaboration.

mistIdeas: Our inference: let a shift of attention move the whole eye pair or head toward a specific target, then hold. Avoid continual wandering that has no apparent object.
Our inference: try quiet listening with a nearly still face and a slight body lean. Contrast will give the next clear reaction more weight.
Our inference: borrow the clarity of silhouette and gaze, not the botanical textures or character shapes.

title: Wirm: a minimal face reacts to falling

people.name: Riley Neville
people.role: Developer; describes making Wirm in a direct 2022 interview

summary: A useful indie comparator because its creator explicitly ties a tiny facial change to a physical event: falling off a rock.

observations.text: Neville describes Wirm's smiling face changing to an open-mouth expression when it falls off a rock. This is direct evidence of an event-driven expression rather than a claim inferred from a trailer.
The inspected official screenshot shows only small dark face marks at the worm's end, while the body drapes over a rock toward a gap. The facial marks remain attached to the body's orientation.

mistIdeas: Our inference: connect surprise to a real interrupt or unexpected outcome, then let the face recover when that condition ends.

Our inference: test the same causal structure with MIST's eyes alone: a brief opening change followed by a stable look at the cause. The mouth is optional; the event relationship is the useful reference.
Our inference: a blink can punctuate the return to listening after surprise, but the sources here do not establish a Wirm blink technique.
